findings.title: Content only appears after JavaScript runs
findings.plain_summary: AI assistants that do not run JavaScript see an empty page.
findings.signal: Visible text length in the raw (pre-JavaScript) HTML response
findings.evidence: Only 55 characters of visible text before JavaScript runs; empty mount node #root; framework markers __NEXT_DATA__
findings.impact: Crawlers that do not execute JavaScript see an empty shell. Facts that only appear after hydration are invisible to them, so nothing is quotable or citable.

suggested_action.summary: Server-render or pre-render the page so its key facts are present in the initial HTML, before any JavaScript runs.
suggested_action.validation: Run `curl -sS file://tests/fixtures/broken_page.html | grep -c "<h1"` and then search the same output for a sentence of your main copy. If the raw HTML does not already contain the text a reader sees, server-side rendering or prerendering is the fix â€” no markup change reproduces it.

findings.title: Mobile viewport is not declared
findings.plain_summary: Your page is not set up to display properly on phones.
findings.evidence: No meta viewport, so the page renders unusably small on mobile — where most AI-referred traffic arrives
findings.impact: Most AI-referred traffic is mobile. Without a viewport declaration the page renders unusably small.

suggested_action.summary: Add <meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1"> so the page renders correctly on phones, where most AI-referred traffic arrives.
suggested_action.snippet:
<!-- In <head>. Without it, mobile browsers render at desktop width and zoom out. -->
<meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1">
suggested_action.validation: Open the page on a phone, or in device emulation, and confirm the text is readable without pinch-zooming.
